meta.asked: the fleet gate MEASURES C# and exits 1 on its fleet-wide bar; this declaration RATCHETS the same measurement per type, so a class can only move deliberately.
meta.metric: ambiguous counted by DECLARATIONS (distinct-file declarations), not distinct kinds
meta.direction: resolved/external are FLOORS (may not decrease). ambiguous/otherUnresolved/unclassed are CEILINGS (may not increase). The classes are siblings that partition the edges: edges = resolved + ambiguous + otherUnresolved + external + unclassed, and the last of those is checked to be 0 rather than assumed.

rules.resolved: target matched exactly one declaration in the 200-file sample's declaration pool (name or qualifiedName alias). A floor, not a ceiling: resolution is the point of the lane.
rules.external: target matched no declaration and the edge carries the analyzer's provable external marker (isExternalTarget:true + a recorded externalReason). A floor: such an edge must keep being able to say so. Marking is NOT claimed complete — see otherUnresolved.
rules.ambiguous: target matched two or more declarations. Counted by DECLARATION (incoming-gate.ts) — a name declared in n files counts n. The pool is file-local, so a member name emitted unqualified by one file can collide with another file's declaration of the same word.
rules.otherUnresolved: target matched no declaration and carries no marker. This is the backlog. It is explicitly NOT asserted to be third-party: each name in it is either (a) a member path of a foreign type the analyzer cannot see, (b) a local declaration question the target spelling defeats, or (c) project code not present in the 200-file sampled pool.
rules.unclassed: edges with an empty target string. Ceiling 0, always: the instrument can only classify an edge it has a target for, and an empty target is a defect in the emitting type, not a class.

notes: A ceiling is a claim about what is known and accepted, never that the class is fine. Repaying a cluster means lowering its ceiling in the same commit that lowers the number.

This gate shares the instrument with the fleet gate on purpose: two instruments measuring the same population and disagreeing is the failure mode script/m14/verify-honesty.ts exists to catch. One measurement, two verdicts — the fleet's bar and Csharp's declaration.
The worklist printed below each type is the instrument's own (up to 25 names per type, per run). A count that cannot be walked back to its names is not a measurement.

EXTERNAL IS 0 on all ten types, and that is a state, not a defect claim: this lane's analyzer emits no provable external marker, so by construction every unbound target in it is backlog (cli/unknown targets included) and the ceiling carries the whole weight. Marking is future work with a proof obligation the Java precedent shows how to meet: an edge may only join the external class if the analyzer can record WHY the target is outside the project (see real-java-analyzer.ts's isExternalTarget + externalReason), because an unmarked unresolved edge and a marked one are different claims.

IMPORTS IS 0 EDGES on this walk. The instrument's `imports` row counts relationship-channel rows only (`imports`/`brain_import`). C# carries its import SITES on the analyzer's separate `imports[]` channel (`ImportInfo[]` → the brain_import table, mirrored as `references` edges marked isImport:true), so for that lane the zero is a CHANNEL fact, not an absence — see real-csharp-analyzer.md's channel table. Where a lane carries no import channel at all, the zero is a lane truth instead; either way the ratchet locks it.

ZERO-EDGE TYPES on this walk: imports. Each is a LOCK, not automatically a gap — floors and ceilings are 0, so the type cannot move without a deliberate re-declaration. A zero can be a recorded ruling (python's `implements` is RULED, falsification in its canonical doc), a channel fact (see the imports note when import sites travel on the analyzer's own channel), or simply absent from this 200-file stride sample (go's `overrides` fires 78 times over the corpus). Read it against the lane's canonical doc before calling it a gap.

qualifiedNameAliases 0: this lane publishes no qualified names, so the qualified-endpoint resolution rule (java's qualifiedNameAliases 3,040) has nothing to bind with here and every alias-shaped target stays unbound by rule rather than by accident.
resolution_caveats: RESOLVED IS NOT 'THE EDGE POINTS AT THE RIGHT DECLARATION' IN THIS LANE. collRes is OF resolved: the target had MORE THAN ONE declaration, so production's own-file tie-break CHOSE the row. A resolved edge in this lane is 'the edge points at A declaration, and where there was more than one, at the one the tie-break chose'. The gate's own TABLE 1 prints, in every lane's log, that the indexer measures a large share of those tie-break picks as WRONG - so the resolved count is a FLOOR on correct resolution and the tie-break's picks are its largest soft spot. The per-row movement of that tie-break is measured directly by script/m14/csharp-tiebreak-movement.ts, not by this count.

THE AMBIGUITY IS PER-PROJECT, AND THAT IS WHY THE POOLED NUMBER IS A DIFFERENT NUMBER. Production resolves a bare name only when its declaration count IN THAT PROJECT is exactly 1, and a qualified name only on an exact project-scoped match; a name that collides in ANOTHER project is NOT ambiguous to production. So TABLE 2 (one pooled corpus key space) and TABLE 1 (per project, the verdict's scope) disagree by construction, and only TABLE 1 is the verdict. A reader comparing this lane's buckets with a lane measured in a pooled key space is comparing two different measurements.

THE CHUNKED MEASUREMENT'S SCOPE IS PROJECT-SCOPED WHILE THE POPULATION IS GLOBAL. Every admitted file is measured exactly once across the chunks, so the EDGE buckets are the population's and are unbiased. But a collision in the half that is not in the slice is invisible, so the name reads unique and the edge resolves: the chunk sum's resolved is BIASED UP and its unresolved and amb(decl) are BIASED DOWN. The chunks TILE THE GLOBAL ADMITTED LIST (offsets 0, N, 2N, ... contiguous) - that is the GLOBAL form, a LOOSER form than the dart lane's per-repository contiguity check, and the number must not be read as a per-repository population.

amb(kind) IS A SUBSET OF amb(decl) AND IS REPORTED BESIDE IT, NEVER ADDED; collRes IS A SUBSET OF resolved AND IS REPORTED BESIDE IT, NEVER ADDED. The closure is resolved + amb(decl) + unresolved + bindOK + bind? + bindFAIL + extOK + ext? + extFAIL + causeOK + causeFAIL = edges, and unclassed is 0 always.

THIS LANE'S `external` BUCKET IS THE EXTERNAL CLAIMS: extOK (the project CONFIRMS the claim) PLUS ext? (a claim no check can reach). A nonzero external is therefore partly a CLAIM, and a claim is a floor like a resolution - it can lose that status. EXTERNAL IS 0 ON EVERY TYPE EXCEPT imports, and that is a STATE, not a defect claim: this lane's analyzer emits no provable external marker for calls/uses/references, so every unbound target in them is BACKLOG and the ceiling carries the whole weight. An unmarked unresolved edge and a marked one are different claims and must not be pooled.

THE `imports` ROW IS A CHANNEL FACT, NOT AN ABSENCE. C# carries its import SITES on the analyzer's separate imports[] channel (ImportInfo[] -> the brain_import table, mirrored as references edges marked isImport:true), so the imports RELATIONSHIP row is 0 while the import sites exist and are counted elsewhere. Reading the imports row as 'C# has no imports' would be wrong; it says the channel is empty, and the channel is the one thing that is empty.

causeOK IS A STATED REASON, NEVER A RESOLUTION. It is bucket 3: the target names nothing here and the edge DECLARED why it could not reach the base, so it is stated rather than claimed - and it is folded into otherUnresolved in this declaration's five-bucket shape, never into resolved.

THE RATCHET DIRECTION. resolved and external are FLOORS (they may not decrease); ambiguous, otherUnresolved and unclassed are CEILINGS (they may not increase). A ceiling is a claim about what is known and accepted, never that the class is fine.
